title: How Life Insurers Can Turn Legacy Conversion into a Modernization Advantage
summary: Learn how life insurers can turn legacy system conversion into a modernization advantage with lower risk, better data readiness and faster paths to value.
body_markdown:
For life insurance carriers, consolidating multiple legacy policy administration systems into a single modern platform offers significant operational, financial, and strategic advantages. Specifically, legacy consolidation allows life insurers to cut costs, improve data quality, enhance customer and agent experiences, accelerate innovation, and position themselves for long-term growth.


However, many carriers that stand to benefit greatly from legacy consolidation have hesitated. Perceived risks, including potential operational disruption (due to data quality/completeness), and a lack of transparency and expertise around legacy platforms often prompt carriers to delay the many benefits they could achieve through conversion. But more carriers are now finding the upfront investment in modernization pays off through sustained operational efficiency and competitive advantage.


Conversion is no longer a leap of faith; with the right architecture, operating model, and automation, it becomes a sequence of proofs and a faster path to reaping a return on investment.


## From legacy constraints to measurable value


For life insurers, conversion is no longer simply a technology obligation; it’s a practical opportunity to reduce legacy drag while improving operating economics and unlocking enterprise value.


Proceeding with conversion can help insurers lower system exposure and reduce ongoing maintenance costs while lessening dependence on scarce institutional knowledge. It also creates a stronger data foundation for automation, analytics, and AI. Carriers with modern platforms such as Verisk’s FAST are increasing their return by bringing more products, policies, and business processes onto their modern platform.


The strongest incentive is economic: each successful conversion can reduce legacy dependency and strengthen the modern platform business case. Moving the next block then becomes easier.


## Cutting execution risk with stronger tools and transparency


Modern platform architecture, improved tooling, and AI-enabled capabilities are lowering the barriers that once made conversion feel too risky.


FAST gives insurers a flexible, configuration-driven destination that supports simplification, reuse, and operational governance. Modern reconciliation, testing, and automation capabilities improve visibility and reduce manual effort while helping resolve issues earlier. Meanwhile, AI can enhance discovery, mapping, data validation, testing, and knowledge capture throughout the conversion life cycle.


Risk isn’t deferred to cutover; it’s retired incrementally through earlier visibility, automated reconciliation, and repeated proof points.


## A conversion ecosystem built to scale


Life insurers don’t need to approach conversion as a one-off, custom effort; FAST has built a repeatable model on a capable platform that delivers enabling tools and domain expertise supported by partner scale.


Continued investment in Verisk’s proprietary Maestro and Maestro+ is advancing AI-enabled conversion. Reusable accelerators, mapping assets, test libraries, and reconciliation capabilities provide support. Insurers can coordinate Verisk, customer, and partner teams around shared objectives, governance, and measurable outcomes to confidently pursue more structured and repeatable conversion processes.


A disciplined program turns conversion work into reusable assets, so the second conversion should be faster than the first, and the tenth faster than the second.


## Matching the path to business priorities


Conversion doesn’t require a single, rigid approach; life insurers can select a strategy within their execution capacity and risk appetite that aligns with their business case and technology environment.


Modern tooling supports phased, block-based, and enterprise consolidation strategies, allowing insurers to sequence work around financial priorities, complexity, timeline requirements, and risk tolerance. Across each model, delivery can be anchored in proof points, transparency, repeatability, and outcome measurement.


The decision shifts from “Can we convert everything?” to “Which blocks create the strongest economic and strategic case?”


## Why now is the time


Life insurers have a compelling reason to act now: the value case for conversion is stronger, and the capabilities available to execute it are more mature than ever.


By proceeding with conversion, insurers can move faster and more confidently to:


- Retire legacy constraints
- Strengthen operational resilience
- Improve data readiness
- Accelerate modernization


FAST is positioned to help customers move forward with a structured, scalable, and value-driven approach.


The old question was whether a carrier could survive conversion; the better question is how quickly it can turn conversion into a repeatable capability. Can your legacy platform support your business objectives?
